clue.text: Kudos! You finally solved a puzzle

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word just before it
a puzzle solved has been worked out, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is congratulated for at last cracking a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The congratulation is the fodder: KUDOS plus the U ending 'You', rearranged, gives SUDOKU.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a popular number-placement grid game, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Sneaky to rip off your former following

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the one before it in the answer

blocks.note: to rip off is to steal

explanation.surface: Copying an ex's admirers looks underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your former' is not an ex but the old word for your, THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means acting quietly and covertly to avoid notice, which is sly or furtive.

clue.text: Look in a guide about communication

indicators.note: in places the interjection inside the other letters
about can mean moved around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone checks a guidebook for advice on communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation between people, an exchange of words, so a form of talk.

clue.text: Birds briefly peck around the edges

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word for peck is dropped
the edges points to the outside letters only of the word just read
around says the shortened word goes outside the remaining letters

blocks.note: a peck is a kiss, cut short
the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Birds peck around the borders of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the edges' does double duty: 'the' is the source and 'edges' tells you to keep its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kites are birds of prey of the hawk family, so they are an example of the category.

clue.text: Resist engagement being cancelled?

blocks.note: a military engagement is a battle
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: A wedding is called off, read as a question about resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement being cancelled' suggests a broken betrothal; read as a battle that is off, it splits into the two parts of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight off an attacker or illness is to repel or hold it back successfully.

clue.text: Popular finishing round on practice green

indicators.note: finishing picks out the last letter of the word that follows
on here means added on to, so the end letter is tacked after the practice word

explanation.surface: A golfer completes a popular round on the practice putting green.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing scene makes 'green' look like part of a course; it is the definition, meaning new to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone naive and untried, lacking the skill that comes from practice.

clue.text: Woman gets bad vibe eating alternative to rabbit, for instance

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word are spoilt into another order
eating takes something inside, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

explanation.surface: A woman feels uneasy eating something other than rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating alternative to rabbit' reads as a meal; in fact the rabbit is the definition, an animal that eats plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits feed only on plants, so they are an example of a plant-eating animal.

clue.text: Last letters heading off from Rome reflected decline

indicators.note: the head is the front, so taking it off removes the opening letter of the city
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the city without its first letter
to sag is to droop or decline

explanation.surface: Final letters sent from Rome reflect the city's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so its plural fits 'Last letters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet, so omegas are final letters.

clue.text: Some of life's terrors get worse

indicators.note: some of says only a part of the following words is needed

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The fears of life grow worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound or a grievance that festers deteriorates, becoming more infected or bitter over time.

clue.text: One time performance is flawless

blocks.note: a one-time partner is an ex
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A critic praises a single past performance as perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact is precise and correct in every detail, hence without any error.

clue.text: Game over before getting to grips with first level is not fun

indicators.note: to do something over is to redo it, so the short word for before is remade in a new order
first picks out the opening letter of the following word
to get to grips with something is to grasp it, so the game holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A game that has ended before its first round even got going is no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game over' reads as one phrase, but 'over' works on 'before'; ere is the poetic word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means gloomy and joyless, which is the same as lacking any enjoyment.

clue.text: I bet that potential winner in front is raring to go

indicators.note: potential means not yet formed, so these letters could still be made into something else
in front puts this piece at the start of the answer

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a racehorse leading the field and eager to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential winner' reads as one phrase, but 'potential' belongs to 'I bet that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Champing at the bit describes a horse, or person, impatient and eager to start.

clue.text: Hurry to watch son on instrument

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent hurries off to see their son play an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is a British imperative meaning be quick, get a move on.

clue.text: Trendy article about space is mindless

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for space is read backwards

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A fashionable magazine piece about outer space is dismissed as brainless.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em; here it is turned round after IN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes talk or behaviour that is silly and lacking sense or thought.

clue.text: Bird box sheltered by terrace?

indicators.note: something sheltered by another is held within it, so the terrace wraps round

blocks.note: a terrace is a row of houses joined together

explanation.surface: A nesting box for birds is tucked against a terrace of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrace is a British row of joined houses, so it supplies HOUSE ... ROW; the question mark admits that loose phrase. Box is the verb, as in sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is a common small brown bird that nests around buildings.

clue.text: I get manic about puzzling!

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the preceding letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver confesses to getting frantic over puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic describes something mysterious and hard to understand, so baffling.

clue.text: Worrying about looking after eggs

blocks.note: first meaning: fretting gloomily over something
second meaning: what a hen does sitting on her clutch

explanation.surface: Someone frets over the care of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dwelling anxiously on troubles and a hen sitting on eggs to hatch them.

clue.text: German article about break point for Rolling Stones?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the German word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: the masculine definite article in German
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A German music article covers the Rolling Stones' break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The band is a red herring: from the proverb, a rolling stone gathers no moss, so it is a person who never settles.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifters move from place to place without roots, just as a rolling stone does in the proverb.

clue.text: Naughty child set fire to model, given permission by mistake

blocks.note: lit is the past of light
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A child set fire to a model, having been allowed to by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' gives T, from Ford's Model T. Permission given is LET, the past sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Little terror is an affectionate idiom for a badly behaved youngster who causes trouble.

clue.text: Boasted that credit's due

explanation.surface: Someone bragged that they deserve the credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag loudly and triumphantly, as a cockerel sounds off, so it equals bragged.

clue.text: Lewd about sailors half-stripped!

indicators.note: something stripped has its outer layer removed, so only the inner letters of the word stay

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of sailors with half their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-stripped' looks like a state of undress, but it is the word 'half' with its outer letters stripped away.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal relates to bodily and sexual desire, so it overlaps with lustful or lewd.

clue.text: Kingdom has bona fide munificent leader

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

explanation.surface: A kingdom boasts a genuine, generous ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a territory ruled by a monarch, the same thing as a domain under a king.

clue.text: Annoyed, when unscrupulous journalist and editor get zero fines

blocks.note: a hack is a disreputable writer for the press
the figure looks like the letter
F is fine (as on pencils), doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone is cross that a shady reporter and his editor escape without any penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for fine, as in pencil grading, and doubling a letter abbreviation makes a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked off is British slang for irritated or fed up, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Eel artfully pierced by silver bird of prey

indicators.note: artfully means with craft, so the letters are skilfully rearranged
something pierced has another thing driven into it, so the scrambled letters surround it

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An eel is skewered by a silver bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large hunting raptor, a classic example of a predatory bird.

clue.text: Retired and moved to live with daughter

blocks.note: went is the past of go

explanation.surface: A pensioner gives up work and moves in with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means turning in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go off to sleep at night, so the phrase for that fits.

clue.text: For example, going back round edge reveals dirt

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the other direction, so the abbreviation is read backwards
round means encircling, so the reversed letters go either side of the next piece

explanation.surface: Turning something over reveals the dirt round its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is ingrained dirt or soot, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Elegant citadel's destroyed by end of battle

indicators.note: a building destroyed is knocked down, so its letters can be rebuilt in a fresh order
end of picks out the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A graceful fortress is ruined at the close of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate describes something fine, dainty and refined in form, close to graceful.

clue.text: Joins forces with foreign gendarmes extracting DNA

indicators.note: extracting means pulling something out, so the named letters are removed from the police word
foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: French police officers, taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Detectives team up with French police to take a DNA sample.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D, N and A out of GENDARMES, leaving GERMES, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or unite with another body, so it amounts to joining together.
